chapter.name: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

subtopics.name: Acidic and Basic Strength of Organic Compounds

questions.stem:
Arrange the following compounds in decreasing order of their basic strength:
(I) Aniline  
(II) $p$-Nitroaniline  
(III) $p$-Methylaniline  
(IV) $p$-Methoxyaniline  

Choose the correct option:
questions.solution:
Electron-donating groups increase the basic strength of aniline, while electron-withdrawing groups decrease it.  
- $-\mathrm{OCH_3}$ (in IV) is a strong $+M$ group (highest basic strength).  
- $-\mathrm{CH_3}$ (in III) is $+I$ and hyperconjugative (higher than aniline).  
- Aniline (I) has no substituents.  
- $-\mathrm{NO_2}$ (in II) is a strong $-M$ group (lowest basic strength).  
Hence, order is IV > III > I > II.

questions.stem:
Among the following compounds, the total number of compounds which are more acidic than benzoic acid is ____________.
- $o$-Nitrobenzoic acid
- $p$-Nitrobenzoic acid
- $p$-Methoxybenzoic acid
- $o$-Toluic acid
- $p$-Toluic acid
- $o$-Bromobenzoic acid
questions.solution:
Due to ortho-effect, ortho-substituted benzoic acids ($o$-nitrobenzoic acid, $o$-toluic acid, $o$-bromobenzoic acid) are more acidic than benzoic acid.
For para-substituted:
- $p$-Nitrobenzoic acid has strong electron-withdrawing $-M$ and $-I$ effects, making it more acidic than benzoic acid.
- $p$-Methoxybenzoic acid is less acidic than benzoic acid due to $+M$ effect of $-\mathrm{OCH_3}$.
- $p$-Toluic acid is less acidic than benzoic acid due to $+I$ and hyperconjugation of $-\mathrm{CH_3}$.
Thus, $o$-nitrobenzoic acid, $p$-nitrobenzoic acid, $o$-toluic acid, and $o$-bromobenzoic acid (total 4) are more acidic than benzoic acid.

questions.stem:
The correct decreasing order of basic strength of the following amines in aqueous solution is:

(I) $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2NH}$
(II) $\mathrm{CH_3NH_2}$
(III) $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3N}$
(IV) $\mathrm{NH_3}$
questions.solution: For methyl-substituted amines in aqueous medium, the basic strength order is determined by inductive effect, steric hindrance, and solvation. The experimentally observed order of basic strength is: secondary > primary > tertiary > ammonia, which corresponds to $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2NH} > \mathrm{CH_3NH_2} > \mathrm{(CH_3)_3N} > \mathrm{NH_3}$ (i.e., I > II > III > IV).

questions.stem:
Among the following, the total number of compounds/species which are more basic than aniline is ___________.
o-toluidine, p-toluidine, m-toluidine, benzylamine, p-nitroaniline, acetanilide, cyclohexylamine
questions.solution:
Comparing basicity with aniline ($pK_b \approx 9.4$):
- o-toluidine is weaker than aniline due to ortho effect.
- p-toluidine is stronger due to $+\mathrm{I}$ and hyperconjugation of $-\mathrm{CH}_3$ group (1).
- m-toluidine is stronger due to $+\mathrm{I}$ of $-\mathrm{CH}_3$ group (2).
- Benzylamine has aliphatic amine character, so much stronger (3).
- p-Nitroaniline is weaker due to strong $-\mathrm{M}$ of $-\mathrm{NO}_2$.
- Acetanilide is weaker because lone pair is delocalized into carbonyl group.
- Cyclohexylamine is an aliphatic amine, so much stronger (4).
Total = 4.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds has the highest acidic strength?
questions.solution: The nitro group ($-NO_2$) is a strong electron-withdrawing group showing $-M$ and $-I$ effects. In $p$-nitrophenol, the $-M$ effect of the $-NO_2$ group strongly stabilizes the phenoxide ion formed after deprotonation. In $m$-nitrophenol, only the $-I$ effect is active. $p$-Cresol has an electron-donating methyl group ($+I$, hyperconjugation) which destabilizes the conjugate base. Thus, $p$-nitrophenol is the most acidic.

questions.stem:
Among the following compounds, the total number of compounds containing at least one $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom is _________.
Benzene, Cyclohexane, Toluene, Acetylene, Ethane, Nitrobenzene, Acetone, Phenol
questions.solution:
- Benzene: all $sp^2$
- Cyclohexane: all $sp^3$ (contains $sp^3$)
- Toluene: methyl carbon is $sp^3$ (contains $sp^3$)
- Acetylene: all $sp$
- Ethane: all $sp^3$ (contains $sp^3$)
- Nitrobenzene: all $sp^2$
- Acetone: two methyl carbons are $sp^3$ (contains $sp^3$)
- Phenol: all $sp^2$
Total compounds containing $sp^3$ hybridized carbons = 4 (Cyclohexane, Toluene, Ethane, Acetone).

questions.stem:
The correct order of increasing basic strength of the following amines in aqueous solution is:
$$\mathrm{(CH_3)_2NH\ (I),\ \ CH_3NH_2\ (II),\ \ (CH_3)_3N\ (III),\ \ NH_3\ (IV)}$$
questions.solution:
In aqueous medium, the basic strength of methyl substituted amines is determined by inductive effect, solvation effect, and steric hindrance. The correct experimental order of basic strength is:
Secondary > Primary > Tertiary > Ammonia\ni.e., $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2NH > CH_3NH_2 > (CH_3)_3N > NH_3}$. Thus: $\mathrm{IV < III < II < I}$.

questions.stem:
The correct increasing order of basic strength for the following compounds is:
(I) Aniline  
(II) $p$-Nitroaniline  
(III) $p$-Methylaniline  
(IV) $p$-Methoxyaniline
questions.solution:
Electron-donating groups increase the basic strength of aniline, while electron-withdrawing groups decrease it.
- $-\mathrm{OCH_3}$ (in IV) is strongly activating via $+M$.
- $-\mathrm{CH_3}$ (in III) is activating via $+I$ and hyperconjugation.
- $-\mathrm{NO_2}$ (in II) is strongly deactivating via $-M$.
Therefore, the basic strength order is: II < I < III < IV.

questions.stem:
The total number of compounds among the following which are more acidic than phenol is _______.
o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol, p-nitrophenol, o-cresol, p-cresol, o-nitrophenylacetic acid, acetic acid
questions.solution:
Comparing acidities with phenol:
- Nitrophenols (o-, m-, and p-nitrophenol) are more acidic than phenol due to electron-withdrawing $-\text{NO}_2$ groups.
- Cresols (o- and p-cresol) are less acidic due to electron-releasing methyl groups.
- Carboxylic acids (acetic acid and o-nitrophenylacetic acid) are much more acidic than phenol.
Thus, more acidic than phenol: o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol, p-nitrophenol, o-nitrophenylacetic acid, and acetic acid (total 5).

questions.stem:
The correct order of acidic strength of the following substituted phenols is:
(I) Phenol 
(II) p-Nitrophenol 
(III) m-Nitrophenol 
(IV) p-Methylphenol
questions.solution:
- Nitro group is electron-withdrawing. At para-position (II), it exerts both $-I$ and $-M$ effects. At meta-position (III), it exerts only $-I$ effect. Thus, II > III.
- Methyl group (IV) is electron-donating via $+I$ and hyperconjugation, decreasing acidity relative to phenol (I).
- Hence, the acidic strength order is: II > III > I > IV.

questions.stem:
Arrange the following compounds in decreasing order of their acidic strength:
(I) Phenol
(II) o-Nitrophenol
(III) m-Nitrophenol
(IV) p-Nitrophenol
questions.solution:
- Nitro group is electron-withdrawing via $-I$ and $-M$ effects at ortho and para positions, while showing only $-I$ at the meta position.
- In o-nitrophenol, intermolecular hydrogen bonding somewhat decreases acidity compared to p-nitrophenol.
- Thus, the order of acidic strength is: p-nitrophenol (IV) > o-nitrophenol (II) > m-nitrophenol (III) > phenol (I).

questions.stem:
Amongst the following, the total number of compounds which are more acidic than benzoic acid is __________.
- $o$-hydroxybenzoic acid
- $p$-nitrobenzoic acid
- $p$-methoxybenzoic acid
- $o$-nitrobenzoic acid
- $p$-methylbenzoic acid
questions.solution:
1. $o$-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid) is much stronger than benzoic acid due to ortho effect and intramolecular H-bonding in conjugate base.
2. $p$-nitrobenzoic acid is more acidic due to the electron-withdrawing $-I$ and $-M$ effects of $-\mathrm{NO}_2$ group.
3. $p$-methoxybenzoic acid is less acidic due to $+M$ effect of $-\mathrm{OCH}_3$.
4. $o$-nitrobenzoic acid is stronger than benzoic acid due to ortho effect.
5. $p$-methylbenzoic acid is less acidic due to $+I$ and hyperconjugative electron donation of $-\mathrm{CH}_3$.
Thus, 3 compounds ($o$-hydroxybenzoic acid, $p$-nitrobenzoic acid, $o$-nitrobenzoic acid) are more acidic.

questions.stem:
The correct order of increasing basic strength of the following compounds in aqueous medium is :
(I) $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$
(II) $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH}$
(III) $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}$
(IV) $\text{NH}_3$
questions.solution:
In aqueous solution, the basic strength of methyl substituted amines depends on inductive effect, solvation effect, and steric hindrance. The correct experimental order is:
$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH} > \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2 > (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N} > \text{NH}_3$.
Thus, in increasing order: $\text{NH}_3 < (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N} < \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2 < (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following molecules has the highest basic strength in aqueous solution?
questions.solution: In aqueous solution, the order of basic strength of methyl substituted amines is: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2NH > CH_3NH_2 > (CH_3)_3N > NH_3}$. Thus, dimethylamine is the strongest base.

questions.stem:
The correct order of acidic strength of the following compounds is:
I. Phenol
II. $p$-Nitrophenol
III. $m$-Nitrophenol
IV. $p$-Methylphenol
questions.solution: Electron withdrawing groups ($-\text{NO}_2$) increase the acidity, while electron donating groups ($-\text{CH}_3$) decrease it. $-\text{NO}_2$ at $p$-position has both $-I$ and $-R$ effects (most acidic), at $m$-position it has only $-I$ effect. Thus, acidity order: $p$-Nitrophenol (II) > $m$-Nitrophenol (III) > Phenol (I) > $p$-Methylphenol (IV).

questions.stem:
Among the following compounds, the number of compounds which are more acidic than benzoic acid is _________.
$o$-Nitrobenoic acid, $p$-Nitrobenzoic acid, $o$-Methylbenzoic acid, $p$-Methylbenzoic acid, $p$-Methoxybenzoic acid
questions.solution:
Due to ortho-effect, both $o$-nitrobenzoic acid and $o$-methylbenzoic acid are stronger acids than benzoic acid.
Due to the $-I$ and $-M$ effect of the $-NO_2$ group, $p$-nitrobenzoic acid is also more acidic than benzoic acid.
$p$-Methylbenzoic acid ($+I$ and hyperconjugation) and $p$-methoxybenzoic acid ($+M$ of $-OCH_3$) are weaker acids than benzoic acid.
Thus, there are 3 compounds more acidic than benzoic acid.

questions.stem:
The correct order of acidic strength of the following substituted phenols is:
(I) $p$-nitrophenol
(II) $p$-cresol
(III) $p$-chlorophenol
(IV) phenol
questions.solution: $-\mathrm{NO_2}$ is a strong electron-withdrawing group ($-M, -I$), which increases acidic strength significantly. $-\mathrm{Cl}$ is electron-withdrawing via $-I$, making $p$-chlorophenol more acidic than phenol. $-\mathrm{CH_3}$ in $p$-cresol is electron-donating ($+I, \text{hyperconjugation}$), decreasing acidity below that of phenol. Thus, the order is I > III > IV > II.

questions.stem:
Amongst the following, the number of compounds which will give a positive test with Tollens' reagent is ________.
(a) Acetaldehyde
(b) Benzaldehyde
(c) Acetone
(d) Fructose
(e) Glucose
(f) Sucrose
(g) Formic acid
questions.solution:
Tollens' reagent is reduced by aldehydes (acetaldehyde, benzaldehyde), reducing sugars (fructose, glucose), and formic acid (due to its oxidizable aldehydic $-\mathrm{CHO}$ like group).
Sucrose (non-reducing sugar) and acetone (ketone) do not react.
Positive test given by: (a), (b), (d), (e), (g) $\implies$ Total of 5 compounds.

questions.stem:
The correct order of increasing basic strength of the following compounds is:

(I) Aniline
(II) $p$-Nitroaniline
(III) $p$-Toluidine
questions.solution: Electron-donating groups like $-\text{CH}_3$ in $p$-toluidine (III) increase the electron density on nitrogen, making it more basic than aniline (I). Electron-withdrawing groups like $-\text{NO}_2$ in $p$-nitroaniline (II) decrease the basicity via resonance and inductive effects. Thus, the order is II < I < III.

questions.stem:
Among the following compounds, the number of compounds which are more acidic than benzoic acid is _________.
(a) $o$-Nitrobenzoic acid
(b) $m$-Nitrobenzoic acid
(c) $p$-Nitrobenzoic acid
(d) $o$-Methylbenzoic acid
(e) $p$-Methylbenzoic acid
(f) $o$-Hydroxybenzoic acid
questions.solution:
Due to the ortho effect, ortho-substituted benzoic acids (except with amino groups) are generally more acidic than benzoic acid. Thus, (a) $o$-nitrobenzoic acid, (d) $o$-methylbenzoic acid, and (f) $o$-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid) are more acidic.
Additionally, electron-withdrawing groups like nitro at meta and para positions increase acidity, making (b) $m$-nitrobenzoic acid and (c) $p$-nitrobenzoic acid more acidic than benzoic acid.
$p$-Methylbenzoic acid (e) has an electron-releasing methyl group which decreases acidity. Hence, 5 compounds are more acidic.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds is the most acidic?
questions.solution: The nitro group is a strong electron-withdrawing group ($-I$ and $-M$ effects), which stabilizes the phenoxide ion through resonance. This makes p-nitrophenol significantly more acidic than phenol and cresols (which contain electron-releasing methyl groups).

questions.stem:
Among the following, the total number of compounds containing at least one $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom is:
(i) Benzene
(ii) Toluene
(iii) Cyclohexane
(iv) Decalin
(v) Ortho-xylene
(vi) Phenol
(vii) Aniline
questions.solution:
Let's examine each compound:
(i) Benzene: All carbons are $sp^2$ hybridized.
(ii) Toluene: The methyl group carbon is $sp^3$ hybridized (1).
(iii) Cyclohexane: All six ring carbons are $sp^3$ hybridized (2).
(iv) Decalin: All ten ring carbons are $sp^3$ hybridized (3).
(v) Ortho-xylene: The two methyl carbons are $sp^3$ hybridized (4).
(vi) Phenol: All carbons in the ring are $sp^2$ hybridized.
(vii) Aniline: All carbons in the ring are $sp^2$ hybridized.
Thus, 4 compounds (toluene, cyclohexane, decalin, ortho-xylene) contain at least one $sp^3$ hybridized carbon.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the strongest base in aqueous solution?
questions.solution: In aqueous solution, the basic strength of methyl-substituted amines follows the order: $2^\circ > 1^\circ > 3^\circ > \mathrm{NH_3}$. Therefore, dimethylamine is the strongest base among the options.

questions.stem:
Among the following compounds, the number of compounds which are more basic than aniline is _______. 
(i) $o$-nitroaniline, (ii) $p$-nitroaniline, (iii) benzylamine, (iv) cyclohexylamine, (v) triphenylamine
questions.solution:
- Aniline has its lone pair conjugated with the benzene ring.
- $o$-nitroaniline and $p$-nitroaniline have strong electron-withdrawing nitro groups, making them less basic than aniline.
- Benzylamine ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$) is aliphatic-like; the lone pair is not conjugated, so it is more basic than aniline.
- Cyclohexylamine is a secondary-like aliphatic amine with no resonance, hence highly basic and more basic than aniline.
- Triphenylamine has its lone pair delocalized over three rings, making it extremely weakly basic.
Thus, only 2 compounds (benzylamine and cyclohexylamine) are more basic than aniline.

questions.stem:
The correct increasing order of acidic strength for the following phenols is:

(I) Phenol 
(II) o-Nitrophenol 
(III) m-Nitrophenol 
(IV) p-Nitrophenol
questions.solution:
The electron-withdrawing $-\mathrm{NO_2}$ group increases the acidity of phenols. 
At meta-position, only $-I$ effect works. At ortho and para positions, both $-I$ and $-R$ effects operate, making them significantly more acidic than m-nitrophenol.
Between o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol, intramolecular hydrogen bonding in o-nitrophenol reduces its proton-donating ability slightly compared to p-nitrophenol.
Thus, the correct sequence is: Phenol (I) < m-Nitrophenol (III) < o-Nitrophenol (II) < p-Nitrophenol (IV).

questions.stem:
The number of groups among the following which are meta-directing when present on a benzene ring is ______________.
$-\text{NO}_2, -\text{OCH}_3, -\text{Cl}, -\text{CN}, -\text{OH}, -\text{COOH}, -\text{COCH}_3, -\text{CHO}, -\text{NH}_2$
questions.solution:
Meta-directing groups (deactivating/electron-withdrawing by $-M$ or $-I$ without $+M$): 
$-\text{NO}_2$, $-\text{CN}$, $-\text{COOH}$, $-\text{COCH}_3$, $-\text{CHO}$.
Total number = 5.
($-\text{OCH}_3$, $-\text{Cl}$, $-\text{OH}$, $-\text{NH}_2$ are ortho/para directing).

questions.stem:
The correct order of basic strength of the following amines in aqueous solution is:
(I) $\mathrm{CH_3NH_2}$
(II) $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2NH}$
(III) $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3N}$
(IV) $\mathrm{NH_3}$
questions.solution: In aqueous medium, the inductive, steric hindrance, and solvation effects collectively decide the basic strength of methyl substituted amines. The correct order is: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2NH > CH_3NH_2 > (CH_3)_3N > NH_3}$. Thus, II > I > III > IV.
